metadata.note: The New York Central's North Country network in northern New York and eastern Ontario -- the branches and connecting roads that surrounded the Adirondack Division (nyc_adirondack_division.geojson) and the Rome, Watertown & Ogdensburg (watertown_rome_railroad.geojson), neither of which covered them. The spine is the Utica & Black River, organized January 29 1853 and built north from Utica in stages (Boonville 1855, Lyons Falls 1867, Lowville 1868, Carthage 1871, Sackets Harbor 1874, Ogdensburg 1878); it was leased to the RW&O in 1886 and passed with it to the New York Central & Hudson River in 1891. Around it the Central gathered the Clayton & Theresa and Ogdensburg & Morristown (both merged into the U&BR in 1886), the Gouverneur & Oswegatchie (first train August 1 1893), and the Carthage & Adirondack mineral branch to Benson Mines and Newton Falls. Separately, a second north-south Adirondack route ran from Moira through St. Regis Falls and Santa Clara to Tupper Lake, and from 1898-1900 was extended north across the St. Lawrence at Cornwall to Ottawa as the New York & Ottawa / Ottawa & New York -- the NYC's Ottawa Division, abandoned February 15 1957. The St. Lawrence & Adirondack carried the Central's Utica-Montreal through trains north from Malone Junction from 1893 until 1953. Passenger service on the Utica-Ogdensburg route ended November 9 1958 and the Utica-Carthage-Watertown 'Bee-Liner' RDC service about 1959-60.

geometry_sources: Wikimedia Commons Data:*.map pages linked from the New York Central Railroad article's system map (CC BY 4.0), themselves derived from OpenStreetMap: New York Central Railroad.map, Mohawk and Malone Railway.map, New York and Ottawa Railway.map. The Utica-Boonville head of the Utica & Black River comes from that map's 'Black River and Utica Railroad' feature; its Utica-Remsen portion deliberately duplicates the Adirondack Division, which ran over the same rails. Geometry used unmodified apart from reversing and chaining LineStrings into through routes; every line was checked against the place-anchor artifact detector and came back clean.
Straight-line chords remain where the source geometry is sparse: up to 7.9 km on the St. Lawrence & Adirondack, 7.4 km on the Ottawa & New York and 4.3 km on the Utica & Black River.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Opening date of the Clayton & Theresa branch (built in the 1870s; the feature starts at the documented 1886 merger into the Utica & Black River). All headways are estimated except the Raquette Lake Railway's sourced two-trains-a-day summer service. End dates for the Clayton, Gouverneur and Philadelphia-Ogdensburg branches are modelled on the November 9 1958 Utica-Ogdensburg discontinuance rather than separately sourced. The New York & Ottawa's crossing of the St. Lawrence at Cornwall is not present in the source geometry, leaving an 8.5 km gap between the Moira-Helena and Cornwall-Ottawa features.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.nyc_company_split: 2026-08-24: compound "predecessor / New York Central Railroad" company strings split per CLAUDE.md Rule 4. The legend groups on the exact company string (app.js railroadsInView), so a compound string drew as a separate railroad from the New York Central even for years the NYC itself ran the trains. Each feature is now split at the date its own segment note names the new operator, into features with identical geometry: the predecessor keeps its name and colour for the earlier years, and the NYC-operated years become "New York Central Railroad" at #5C677D. The Pittsburgh and Lake Erie and the Big Four were renamed but NOT split -- both were NYC-controlled yet stayed separately operated railroads under their own names, so they keep their own legend row.

properties.line: Raquette Lake: Carter (Clearwater) – Raquette Lake
properties.speed_source: estimated: short Adirondack resort branch; unsourced

segments.note: Chartered February 20 1899 by a syndicate of Adirondack great-camp owners -- Durants, Huntingtons, Webbs, Whitneys -- to spare themselves the carry from the Fulton Chain station. Ran July 1 1900 to September 15 1933; two trains a day in summer (one a sleeping-car train), one train a day three days a week in winter. Track lifted 1934. Summer frequency is sourced; the 720-minute headway models the two-train summer service.
